items.title: Section: The Ground of Entry Opens

items.zh: 如是已說種姓地。云何趣入地？嗢拕南曰：若略說一切趣入地，應知謂自性、安立、諸相、數取趣。謂若趣入自性、若趣入安立、若趣入者所有諸相、若已趣入補特伽羅，如是一切總略為一，名趣入地。云何趣入自性？謂安住種姓補特伽羅，本性成就涅槃種子。若於爾時有佛出世，生於中國，不生達須、蔑戾車中，乃至廣說初得見佛及佛弟子，往詣承事，從彼聞法得初正信、受持淨戒、攝受多聞、增長惠捨、調柔諸見。從是已後，由此法受、由此因緣，身滅壞已、度此生已，獲得六處異熟所攝殊勝諸根，能作長時轉勝正信生起依止；亦能與彼受持淨戒、攝受多聞、增長惠捨、調柔諸見，轉上、轉勝、轉復微妙為所依止。復由如是轉上、轉勝、轉復微妙信等諸法，更得其餘殊勝異熟；由此異熟，復得其餘隨順出世轉勝善法。如是展轉互為依因，互與勢力，於後後生轉轉勝進，乃至獲得最後有身。謂住於此得般涅槃，或能趣入正性離生。是名趣入。
items.en: Thus the Ground of Spiritual Lineage has already been explained. What is the Ground of Entry? …If, in brief, one is to explain everything belonging to the Ground of Entry, it should be understood as: intrinsic nature, establishment, marks, and the persons who possess it. …What is the intrinsic nature of entry? It is that a person who abides in lineage, whose nature already possesses the seed of nirvāṇa — should a buddha appear in the world at that time, and should this person be born in a central land … first comes to see the Buddha and the Buddha's disciples, attends and serves them, and from them hears the Dharma, attaining initial pure faith, upholding pure discipline, gathering extensive learning, cultivating growing generosity, and taming and softening [wrong] views. …In this way, [faculties and results] serve, turn by turn, as mutual causes and mutual sources of strength, becoming ever more excellent from one rebirth to the next, until finally the final body of existence is obtained — the body in which nirvāṇa is attained, or in which one enters correct nature free of afflictive arising. This is called entry.

items.zh: 何以故？若道、若路、若正行跡，能得涅槃、能趣涅槃；彼於爾時，能昇、能入、能正行履，漸次趣向，至極究竟。是故說此名已趣入。如是名為趣入自姓。

items.title: Establishing Entry: Four Categories of Dharma, Four Categories of Person

items.zh: 云何建立趣入？謂或有種姓，或有趣入，或有將成熟，或有已成熟。或有唯趣入，非將成熟，非已成熟；或有亦趣入，亦將成熟，非已成熟；或有亦趣入，亦已成熟，非將成熟；或有非趣入，非將成熟，非已成熟。云何有種姓？謂如前說。云何有趣入？謂住種姓補特伽羅，最初獲得昔所未得，於諸如來正覺正說法毘奈耶，所有正信、受持淨戒、攝受多聞、增長惠捨、調柔諸見。是名趣入。云何將成熟？謂即如是已得趣入補特伽羅，除所獲得最後有身。謂住於此得般涅槃，或能趣入正性離生。從趣入後，於後後生修集諸根，轉上、轉勝、轉復微妙。是名將成熟。云何已成熟？謂所獲得最後有身。若住於此得般涅槃，或能趣入正性離生。是名已成熟。
items.en: What is the establishment of entry? There is possessing lineage, having entered, about to ripen, and already ripened. There is one who has only entered, neither about to ripen nor already ripened; one who has both entered and is about to ripen, but is not already ripened; one who has both entered and is already ripened, but is not about to ripen [in the ordinary sense]; and one who has neither entered, nor is about to ripen, nor is already ripened. What is possessing lineage? It is as explained before. What is having entered? It is that a person abiding in lineage, for the first time, attains what was never attained before — pure faith in the Dharma and discipline rightly taught by the perfectly awakened tathāgatas, upholding pure discipline, gathering extensive learning, cultivating growing generosity, and taming and softening [wrong] views. This is called entry. What is about to ripen? It is that this same person, having already attained entry, aside from having obtained the final body of existence … from the time of entry onward, cultivates the faculties from one rebirth to the next, becoming ever more excellent, ever more subtle. This is called about to ripen. What is already ripened? It is having obtained the final body of existence — the body in which, abiding in it, nirvāṇa is attained, or in which one enters correct nature free of afflictive arising. This is called already ripened.

items.zh: 云何唯趣入，非將成熟，非已成熟？謂初獲得於諸如來正覺正說法毘奈耶所有正信，廣說乃至調柔諸見；未從此後復經一生。是名唯趣入，非將成熟，非已成熟。云何亦趣入，亦將成熟，非已成熟？謂初獲得於諸如來正覺正說法毘奈耶所有正信，廣說乃至調柔諸見；從此已後，復經一生，或二、或多，而未獲得最後有身。謂住於此得般涅槃。餘如前說。是名亦趣入，亦將成熟，非已成熟。云何亦趣入，亦已成熟，非將成熟？謂即如是已得趣入補特伽羅，復已獲得最後有身。若住於此得般涅槃，餘如前說。是名亦已趣入，亦已成熟，非將成熟。云何非已趣入，非將成熟，非已成熟？

items.title: Completing the Four-Fold Person-Classification, and a Firm Exclusion

items.zh: 謂即如是有涅槃法補特伽羅，唯住種姓，而未趣入。是名非已趣入，非將成熟，非已成熟補特伽羅。然有堪能，定當趣入、當得成熟。復有一類補特伽羅，定無堪能當得趣入、當得成熟。謂離種姓無涅槃法補特伽羅。當知如是補特伽羅無種姓故，定無堪能當得趣入及當成熟。何況當能得般涅槃。
items.en: It is precisely such a person possessing the dharma of nirvāṇa, abiding in lineage alone, not yet having entered. This is called a person who has neither entered, nor is about to ripen, nor is already ripened — yet who has the capacity, and will certainly enter and attain ripening in time. There is, further, a class of person who definitely has no capacity ever to enter or ever to ripen — namely, a person apart from lineage altogether, lacking the dharma of nirvāṇa. It should be understood that, because such a person lacks lineage, that person definitely has no capacity ever to enter or ever to ripen — let alone ever attain nirvāṇa.

blocks.text: The second part of the Śrāvaka Stage, the **Stage of Entry** (趣入地): how a person with the seed actually begins. One short passage (0400a03) is untranslated.
The summary verse: the Stage of Entry is explained by its nature, its establishment, its marks, and its persons.

One "first comes to see the Buddha and his disciples, attends and serves them, and hears the Dharma from them, attaining initial pure faith", then upholds the precepts, learns widely, practises generosity, and "tames and softens one's views". Venerable Miào Jìng: this last means beginning the five methods for stilling the mind and the four foundations of mindfulness. This first contact plants the seeds that will bring liberation in a later life.

Four categories of dharma and four of person: those who have entered or not, ripened or not, and so on. Venerable Miào Jìng warns: "We say, 'If he lacks the lineage, however you cultivate him he won't succeed.' This is wrong; don't say it. Ordinary people cannot know."

"There is a class of person who definitely has no capacity ever to enter or ripen: a person apart from lineage, lacking the dharma of nirvāṇa." The treatise states the doctrine plainly; the teachers' caution concerns our ability to recognise such a person, which is nil.

quiz.q: Into what four headings does the treatise summarise the Ground of Entry?
options: intrinsic nature, establishment, marks, and persons
quiz.why: The summary verse: if one is to explain the Ground of Entry in brief, it is intrinsic nature, establishment, marks, and persons. Venerable Miào Jìng: the Ground of Hearers has three great parts — lineage, entry, and emancipation.

quiz.q: What does the treatise say the intrinsic nature of entry is?
options: a lineage-bearer meets a buddha, sees and serves the Buddha and disciples, hears the Dharma, and gains initial faith, pure discipline, learning, growing generosity, and softened views
quiz.why: "First comes to see the Buddha and the Buddha's disciples, attends and serves them, and from them hears the Dharma, attaining initial pure faith, upholding pure discipline, gathering extensive learning, cultivating growing generosity, and taming and softening views." Venerable Miào Jìng: faith, discipline, learning, giving, and wisdom — five in all.

quiz.q: What does Venerable Miào Jìng say "taming and softening views" actually involves?
options: practising the five methods for stilling the mind and beginning the four foundations of mindfulness
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "taming and softening views" really means having practised the five stilling methods, beginning the five methods and the four foundations of mindfulness. He adds that only non-self contemplation softens self-view.

quiz.q: Which commonly heard saying does Venerable Miào Jìng call mistaken?
options: "a human birth is hard to gain"
"if he lacks the lineage, no amount of cultivation will work" — one should not say this
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: we say, "If he lacks the lineage, however you cultivate him he won't succeed" — this is wrong; don't say it. Ordinary people cannot judge who lacks lineage.

quiz.q: Which kind of person does the treatise say definitely has no capacity to enter or ripen?
options: one in lineage not yet entered
one apart from lineage, lacking the dharma of nirvāṇa
one born in a border land
quiz.why: "There is, further, a class of person who definitely has no capacity ever to enter or ripen — a person apart from lineage, lacking the dharma of nirvāṇa." One merely in lineage "yet has the capacity, and will certainly enter." Master Cháng Bǎi: where there is a seed there is possibility — capacity is the key.
